subject: Recap + action items: Hosted API evaluation (quickstart, endpoints, rate limits)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia@novalinehealth.com>
Cc: Evan Cole <evan.cole@novalinehealth.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0400
Subject: Recap + action items: Hosted API evaluation (quickstart, endpoints, rate limits)

Hi Amelia / Evan —

Great to meet you on the demo earlier. Thanks for walking us through the Novaline use case — very helpful context. I wanted to recap what we covered and propose straightforward next steps so your engineering team can begin a focused hosted evaluation.

Summary (quick):
- Fit: Hosted API looks like the fastest path to validate latency and cost assumptions for your customer-facing triage assistant. We discussed Dedicated/Private for later if you need strict VPC isolation or formal on-prem requirements.
- Demo highlights: streaming responses, function-style structured outputs, and live latency demos at ~80ms p50 on our sample prompts (demo infra).

What I'm attaching for the pilot: redwood-quickstart-playbook.pdf (step-by-step), hosted-rate-limits-table.csv (defaults + adjustable caps), and demo-api-snippets.txt (curl + SDK snippets).

Proposed hosted quickstart (2-week focused pilot):
1) Create evaluation API key -> run smoke tests using /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings.
2) SE pairing session (30–60m) to run your representative prompts and verify p95 latency and token costs.
3) We'll lift soft rate limits for the pilot to match your target traffic (see below), and capture token/latency breakdowns in the Console.

Default hosted limits and pilot adjustments (we can tune):
- Soft requests: 120 reqs/min per API key (burst to 240).
- Tokens per minute throttle: 250k tokens/min (can be increased for pilot).
- Concurrent inflight requests recommended: start at 10–20 for interactive workloads; scale for batch.

If you're aiming to validate a production-like throughput, tell us your target RPS and average prompt/response size and we'll configure a dedicated concurrency window for the pilot.

Next steps: can you confirm the goal for the 2-week pilot (latency SLO, target daily queries, and any compliance gating like PHI)? Once we have that:
- I’ll provision a scoped API key and enable a 1:1 SE session with Dev.
- We’ll schedule a 30m kickoff next week.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this quickly.

Best,
Logan Wright
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555‑0124

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-playbook.pdf, hosted-rate-limits-table.csv, demo-api-snippets.txt

From: Amelia Ross <amelia@novalinehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Cole <evan.cole@novalinehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 17:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap + action items: Hosted API evaluation (quickstart, endpoints, rate limits)

Thanks Logan — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from the product/engineering side before we lock dates: 

1) Authentication & secrets: is API key auth the only option for the hosted eval? We have a temporary token rotation requirement for the PoC.
2) Data handling: Novaline handles PHI. We heard hosted is possible but we may need either a Private deployment or Dedicated capacity depending on audit needs — can you call out which compliance items require Dedicated/Private vs which are covered on Hosted?
3) Pilot scale: for the pilot we want to emulate 1k QPS spikes (short bursts) to validate throttling behavior — is that realistic for a Hosted pilot or would we need Dedicated to test that traffic profile?

If you can get Dev to confirm the answers and give an example cURL call and pilot provisioning timeline that would help. We’re hopeful Hosted can work for now to move fast.

Amelia
VP Product, Novaline Health
amelia@novalinehealth.com | +1 (212) 555‑0189

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia@novalinehealth.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap + action items: Hosted API evaluation (quickstart, endpoints, rate limits)

Hi Amelia — quick tech notes to address each of your bullets. Happy to dive deeper in the SE pairing session.

1) Auth & rotation:
- Hosted uses bearer API keys by default (Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>).
- For PoCs that require rotation we support short-lived keys via our token service (we can issue keys that rotate every N minutes and show example rotation code).
- I attached demo-api-snippets.txt with a sample rotation flow (node/python).

2) Data handling & compliance:
- Hosted: TLS in transit, encryption at rest, SOC 2 Type II controls, and contractual security addenda available. For PHI-heavy workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private if you need customer-managed KMS/HSM or strict network isolation (VPC peering / private control plane).
- If you need to keep data completely within your VPC, Private (VPC/on-prem) is the option. Dedicated provides isolated GPU pools and tighter tenancy but still uses our control plane. Hosted can be acceptable with a BAAs and stricter contract language for some customers — we'll surface what is and isn't covered.

3) Pilot scale & rate-limiting:
- Hosted can simulate high burst traffic but the default soft limit (120 reqs/min per key) is intentionally conservative. For a runway test at 1k QPS sustained you will likely need Dedicated or a reserved capacity window.
- For your requested short spikes (1k QPS short bursts), we can enable a controlled pilot: provision a temporary elevated quota (e.g., 1k RPS for 15-minute window) and monitor regen behavior. That requires advance notice to reserve capacity and may incur pilot charges.

Quick cURL example (from demo-api-snippets.txt):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <EVAL_API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Summarize patient intake notes","max_tokens":256}'

Next steps I propose:
- Logan to provision an eval key and we set a 30–60m SE pairing in the next 48–72h.
- You share a sample workload (typical prompt size, expected tokens per call, and desired test spike profile).
- We create a pilot plan that includes one scheduled elevated burst window to validate throttling behavior.

Happy to jump on a call — I can do Tue/Wed mornings ET.

–Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai | +1 (646) 555‑0321

Attachment referenced: demo-api-snippets.txt
